analysis: The batch only adds Swift test files: ClusterWaitlistGateTests.swift and FeatureWaitlistTests.swift under provider-swift/Tests/DarkbloomCLITests. No production source changes were in the supplied evidence, so no runtime security regression can be attributed to these units. The tests describe production behavior that is not supplied: a coordinator waitlist gate for new cluster pairs and the sandbox setup, with a FeatureWaitlistClient that sends the login bearer token only to https or loopback coordinators, plus terminal-injection sanitization. The gate's behavior on existing pairings, local-only scope, 404 and error paths is exercised; the tests encode fail-closed behavior for 401, 403 and unreachable answers, with the 404 older-coordinator fallback going on. The tests use fake tokens (eigeninference-pt-waitlist), an invalid coordinator host and stubbed transports, so there are no real secrets and no network access. Relevant threat models are TB-013/T-061 (sandbox setup gating) and TB-014/T-062 (cluster); this PR is test-only, so those boundaries are unchanged. Open integration questions, which need the production sources and cannot be settled from tests: (1) FeatureWaitlistClient.base must really reject non-https remote hosts, as the base() test asserts. (2) The 404 (notOffered) fail-open path lets setup proceed when a coordinator reports no waitlist; this appears to be a product access-gate policy and not a security control, but if the waitlist were intended to enforce authorization, a spoofed or older coordinator could bypass it. The coordinator is trusted. (3) escapingUnprintable and the view sanitization must match the tested behavior; the tests cover OSC 52, C1 CSI and bidi controls, and the bidi override is mapped to U+FFFD. No finding is raised because the production code is unverified, so deeper review of the production sources is warranted.
